purpose: What to build ON. baseline.json answers 'which version'; this answers 'which thing'. Separate files because they change for different reasons - a version ships, a platform choice is a decision.

dataStores.rule: There is no default. Each project chooses its store as a business AND architecture decision from its own facts - primary client, offline needs, real query shapes, cost, and what is already run well. Record the reasoning in that project's CLAUDE.md.
dataStores.theFailureModeThisPrevents: Relational-shaped data forced into Firestore with the joins papered over in Cloud Functions. That is the mismatch to name early, not a reason to avoid Firestore - Firestore is right where it fits, and slotd-web is the worked example.

relational.when: Joins across three or more entities, aggregate reporting, geospatial queries, constraints that must hold across rows, or any schema you would naturally draw as a foreign-key diagram.
relational.rule: SPLIT BY ROLE. The question is never 'which Postgres' - it is 'is this store authoritative'. Answer that first and the vendor follows.

systemOfRecord.why: Same org, IAM and billing as everything else, private IP, and the same region as Cloud Run. Authoritative data does not take a cross-region hop or sit behind another vendor's connection string.
systemOfRecord.auth: IAM + private IP. No connection string to scope.
systemOfRecord.cost: Bills even at idle. That is the deliberate price of authority - if a workload cannot justify it, it probably is not a system of record.

readModel.why: Derived, rebuildable, never authoritative - so cross-region latency and a connection-string secret are acceptable costs, and no idle bill is a real win. PostGIS is ready and the pattern is proven.
readModel.secretRule: Scope SUPABASE_DB_URL to the services that actually query it. slotd-web binds it to 12 callables where only 3 use Postgres; that is the shape to avoid (its P49).

documentRealtime.when: A mobile or offline-first client is the primary consumer, writes must queue locally, or a second actor mutates a record live.
documentRealtime.why: Offline persistence and optimistic writes come free from the SDK. Nothing else in the stack gives that. This is a real strength, not a fallback - slotd-web chose it deliberately for field work and it stays.

readModel.when: A query shape the system of record genuinely cannot serve - radius search, faceting, ranking, reporting rollups.
readModel.pattern: slotd-web discovery/pgProjection.ts is the reference implementation. Rules: the projection write is best-effort and NEVER throws (a derived store must not fail a user's save); it logs at `error` on failure because a swallow is invisible; it no-ops when the secret is unset (that doubles as the rollout switch); and it ships with a rebuild/reconcile script so drift is always repairable.

objectStorage.why: Same org, same IAM, same billing.

cache.why: Nothing here has the traffic to justify Redis. Add it when a measurement says to, not before.

antiPatterns: Modelling relational data in Firestore and papering the joins with Cloud Functions. Name the mismatch early instead of absorbing it in application code.
Making a read model authoritative. If it cannot be dropped and rebuilt from the system of record, it is not a read model.
Reaching for a second database because one query is awkward. Two stores is a permanent tax - pay it only for a shape the first genuinely cannot serve.
Choosing a store because another project uses it. The facts that made it right there may not hold here.

longRunningOrScheduled.use: n8n on naten, or Airflow on the homelab (CT119) for data pipelines
longRunningOrScheduled.note: n8n is the default orchestration layer. Its API is tailnet-only - nothing on CI or Cloud Run can call it. Webhooks are the public surface.

vm.why: One exists (ld-gcp-vm-auto-01) because n8n needs it. A second one needs a real reason.

identity.avoid: minting another service-account JSON key - there are already 9 across two projects

secrets.rule: Secret NAMES live in git, values never. Render into a gitignored file at deploy time; never echo a secret into a transcript.
secrets.ci: GitHub Actions get NO secrets and NO deploy access. Validate-only, by design.

dns.rule: Every DNS change is an OWNER punchlist item - it is a console step an agent cannot perform. Never write a plan step that assumes an agent can add a record.

ai.rule: Target current Claude models. Do not introduce a second model vendor without a stated reason.
ai.note: Vertex AI is enabled-but-dormant on lawn-dart. That is a billing risk, not an available capability.
